lines.text: A man's wisdom brightens his face, and the Teacher says to keep the king's command because of your oath before God.
Do not persist in a bad cause, for the king will do whatever he pleases, and whoever keeps his command will come to no harm.
No man has power over the fire to contain it, and no one has authority over his day of death.
The wicked who used to go in and out of the holy place were buried and cursed in the city.
The Teacher commended the enjoyment of life, since there is nothing better under the sun than to eat and drink and be merry.
